2.

The brief story of the prosecution are as under:

sentences.text: The accused is the husband of the deceased Smt.Firdosh @ Asma.

After marriage,
accused was quarrelling with the deceased in family matters and thereby caused mental and physical torture.
Such being the case, on 25.06.2023 at 10.00 a.m due to the rift between the accused and deceased, the deceased has decided to go to her parental house.
When she expressed the same before the accused, the accused abetted her to go and die.

Due to the reaction of the accused, deceased felt very sad and committed suicide on the same day i.e. on 25.06.2023 between 10.00 a.m. to 4.00 p.m by hanging herself with the help of saree and thereby the accused has committed the offences as alleged against him.
3.
The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the concerned ACMM., Bangalore.
The learned Magistrate has took cognizance of the offences and committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. after furnishing copy of charge sheet to the accused.
The same was numbered as SC No.483/2024.
4. The prosecution has examined eight witnesses as PW.1 to PW.8 and got exhibited documents at Ex.P1 to P13 and M.Os.1 and 2.
On consent of the accused counsel, the inquest Mahazar, P.M.Report and deceased photographs have been marked at Ex.P.1 to 3 respectively.
As such the learned PP gave up the witnesses C.W.7 to 9, 12 to 14.
The prosecution has failed to examine C.W.11 due to the failure of the concerned police to execute warrant and keep the said witness C.W.11 present before the court.
As such prayer of the learned PP was rejected and C.W.11 is dropped as the independent witness turned hostile.

5. After completion of prosecution side evidence, this Court has recorded the statement of accused,
as provided U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.
The accused has denied incriminating evidence present against him and not claimed any defense evidence nor submitted anything to the Court.
The accused has complied application u/s.437A of Cr.PC by executing personal bond and surety bond.

6. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record.
7.

The following points that arises for consideration of this court:
1. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused and deceased-Smt.Firdosh @
Asma are being the husband and wife, the accused subjected deceased to physical and mental cruelty by abusing her in filthy language and thereby accused has committed an offence punishable u/s 498A of IPC?
2. Whether the prosecution proves that accused being the husband of deceased Smt.Firdosh @ Asma, subjected deceased to physical and mental cruelty, on 25.06.2023 at 10.00 a.m due to the rift between the accused and deceased, the deceased has decided to go to her parental house, when she expressed the same before the accused, the accused abetted her to go and die, due to the reaction of the accused, deceased felt very bad and committed suicide on the same day i.e. on 25.06.2023 between 10.00 a.m. to 4.00 p.m by hanging herself with the help of saree Yelahanka New Town P.S vs A1 Sadiq Pasha Alias Mohammed Sadiq on 24 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113315027/

8. This Court has answered the above above points are as under:
 Point No.1: In the Negative  Point No.2: In the Negative  Point No.3: As per final order  for the following:
 R E A S O N S 9. Points Nos.1 and 2: These points are taken up together as they are related to each other and to avoid repetition in the discussion.
The prosecution got examined eight witnesses as P.W.1 to P.W.8 as referred above and got exhibited documents at Ex.P.1 to 13.
On consent of accused counsel, the inquest Mahazar, P.M.Report and deceased photographs marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.3.
The inquest Mahazar and P.M.Report clearly reveals the death of deceased by name Firdosh @ Ashma was due to "Asphyxia as a result of hanging".
The photos marked at Ex.P.3 also supports the documents Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2.
Now, the question before the court is whether the accused has tortured the deceased physically and mentally so that the deceased has committed suicide.

To prove the said allegations, the prosecution examined the mother and brothers of the deceased by name Mumtaz Begum, Syed Pasha, Naveed Pasha,
Sharukh Khan, Mehaboob Pasha, Tabrez as P.W.1 to P.W.6 respectively and pancha by name Abdul Kayoom as P.W.7.
The evidence of P.W.1 to P.W.6 including the complainant PW-1 i.e. mother of the deceased discloses after marriage about 12 years back, the deceased and accused resided together happily.
Due to marital relationship, the deceased has gave birth to a male child.
Both were leading their marital life happily.
But the deceased was suffering from severe headache.
According to the said witness, the accused never tortured the deceased either physically or mentally.
As the deceased suffered severe head ache and unable to bear the same, committed suicide about 2 years back.
When the complainant was in very sad mood due to the death of her daughter, at that time, the police have obtained her signature on complaint marked at Ex.P.4.
She does not know the contents of the complaint.
So also, the witnesses P.W.2 to P.W.6 never supported the story of the prosecution by deposing the similar evidence as deposed by the witness P.W.1.

According to the said witnesses,
accused never tortured the deceased physically or mentally and police have not recorded their statements.
As such, the learned PP has treated the witnesses P.W.1 to P.W.6 as hostile and cross- examined with the permission of the court.
The said witnesses P.W.1 to P.W.6 never admitted the suggestion of the learned PP.
As such, the statements of the witnesses P.W.2 to P.W.6 have been marked at Ex.P.5 to Ex.P.9 respectively.
10. It is necessary to note that the pancha by name Abdul Kayoom examined as P.W.7 also not supported the prosecution story even though he was signatory to the Mahazar Ex.P.10.

According to him, police have obtained his signatures on some documents at his house and not seized any M.Os Yelahanka New Town P.S vs A1 Sadiq Pasha Alias Mohammed Sadiq on 24 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113315027/
3 and thereby not supported the prosecution story.

sentences.text: The Investigation Officer P.W.8 by name Sushma has categorically deposed before the court that on 25.06.2023 at 9.00 p.m complainant came to police station and lodged complaint.
On the basis of the complaint, she has registered Cr.No.191/2023.
Immediately she visited the spot and conducted inquest Mahazar between 9.15 p.m. and 11.00 p.m on the dead body of the deceased as per Ex.P.1.
Thereafter the said dead body was shifted to the mortuary of Dr.Ambedkar Hospital, on the same day she has recorded statements of the C.W.5 and C.W.6 as per Ex.P.8 and Ex.P.9.
Thereafter she deputed C.W.13 and C.W.14 to trace the accused.
On the same day, at 11.30 p.m. the police staffs C.W.13 and C.W.14 produced the accused before her alongwith report as per Ex.P.12.
On 26.06.2023, she submitted requisition to the Medical Officer to conduct Post Mortem on the dead body of the deceased.

After completion of the post mortem she handed over the dead body to its family members and obtained acknowledgement and she has also taken photographs as per Ex.P.3 when the dead body was in the hospital.
She has produced accused before the court alongwith remand application after medical examination.
On the same day, C.W.14 has produced the clothes of the deceased and same were seized under Mahazar marked at Ex.P.10.

She has brought the said clothes into P.F.No.95/2023 and identified the same,
the said clothes of the deceased marked at M.O.1 and M.O.2.
On 05.07.2023 she has collected P.M.Report.
On 21.10.2023, the accused Nos.2 to 4 appeared before her alongwith the bail order of the court.
She has carried out arrest procedure against accused Nos.2 to 4 and released them on bail on 10.11.2023.
She has submitted charge sheet against accused No.1.
The said evidence of the Investigation Officer has completely denied by the accused counsel.
The evidence given by the Investigation Officer not match with the evidence of any independent witnesses including pancha examined by the prosecution.
So, it is very clear that the prosecution has completely failed to prove the allegations made against the accused as alleged against him.
As such, this court has answered the Point Nos.1 and 2 in the Negative.
11. Point No.3:

In view of answer of this court on points No.1 and 2, this court proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 306 of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bond of accused stands cancelled.
The M.O.1 and M.O.2 being clothes of deceased are being worthless , are ordered to be destroyed after appeal period is over.
